images.title: Paying for college in the right order
images.alt: Order for covering college costs: complete the FAFSA, use grants and scholarships, take federal loans, try other options, then borrow privately for the gap.
images.caption: A private loan is a reasonable way to cover the last part of the bill, not the first.

items.title: Complete the FAFSA
items.text: Fill it out even if you expect to get little.

items.title: Take federal loans
items.text: Fixed rates, mostly no credit check, and repayment protections.

items.title: Try other options
items.text: More scholarships, an aid office review, a payment plan, part-time work.

items.title: Borrow privately for the gap
items.text: Only for whatever is still left.

images.title: Fixed or variable rate
images.alt: Comparison of fixed and variable private student loan rates: fixed stays the same, variable follows a market index and can rise or fall.
images.caption: For a loan carried ten years or more, lean fixed unless you expect to pay it off quickly.

columns.label: Fixed rate
points: Same rate for the life of the loan
Suits loans carried ten years or more

columns.label: Variable rate
points: Often starts lower, can rise or fall

images.title: Work out your gap
images.alt: Flow for sizing a private student loan: start with cost of attendance, subtract aid and federal loans, subtract family contribution, borrow only the gap.
images.caption: Borrow the gap and no more, and confirm there's no prepayment penalty before you sign.
images.note: Rule of thumb: keep total student debt below expected first-year earnings

items.label: Cost of attendance
items.text: Start with the school's full figure.

items.label: Minus aid
items.text: Subtract every grant, scholarship and federal loan.

items.label: Minus family funds
items.text: Subtract what the family can pay from income and savings.

items.label: The gap
items.text: What's left is the most to borrow privately.
